Commentary.Commentary: 339 looks to be a bit beyond Ireland's reach. Given the way the ball spun in the first innings, the Afghan spinners should enjoy bowling on this pitch, especially Rashid Khan. However, if the chasing side gets off to a good start, you never know. Join us back at 1345 local (0815 GMT).

Not a great outing with the ball for the Irish. Dockrell held one end up with figures of 2/45 in 10 overs while Paul Stirling had a lottery - 6 wickets in 10 overs. Poor Peter Chase missed his century by just 8 runs.

Rahmat Shah played a lovely knock of 68 while skipper Asghar Stanikzai made a terrific 101. He held the innings from one end, ensuring that Afghanistan do not throw away the set platform. Towards the end, Shafiqullah Shafaq's cameo of 35 from 17 balls took the total close to 340.

Mohammad Shahzad got off to a flier, with a quickfire 63 from 43 balls before Dockrell trapping him LBW. But that was after the openers added 90 in 14 overs. Then there were a couple of decent stands for the third and fourth wicket. That was followed by a mild collapse in the middle but that was more because the batsmen were going for quick runs.

A terrific batting display from Afghanistan. This is their best ODI total and just their second over 300. It all started from the very beginning with the Afghan openers not letting the Irish settle at all.

OUT! A six for Stirling! Floated outside off, Dawlat gets down and attempts the slog sweep. Unfortunately, he is not able to clear the man at long on. William Porterfield judges the catch to perfection at the ropes and leaps at the right time to take the catch.  Paul Stirling does not even celebrate. Best ODI figures for him. AFGHANISTAN HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 338.

Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
FOUR! Kaboom! Half volley outside off, Shahzad smashes it over mid off and makes Chase pay for that extra delivery. 17 from the over, 30 off the last 2!

NO BALL, FOUR! Chase goes for the extra yard of pace and oversteps. Bowls it short and hurries the batsman who is already through with his pull shot. His right hand comes off the bat and he is no control. But still the ball wallops off the bat through square leg to the fence.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

EDGED, FOUR! Unlucky for the bowler. He bowls this on a fuller length outside off, gets the outside edge as Shahzad looks to defend but the ball flies past first slip, through the vacant second slip region to the third man fence.
Nicely played. Uses his wrists and wrestles this from outside off through mid-wicket. By the time fine leg can get across, three runs are taken.
Another mix-up. Noor Ali taps this towards cover and sets off for a single but is sent back. Already there has been plenty of miscommunication between these two batsmen.
On a length around middle and off, tucked behind square leg for a single.

FOUR! Stunning shot. Overpitched outside off, Noor Ali comes forward and drives this with a straight back, right past the bowler. Murtagh sticks out his right leg but the ball races away like a tracer bullet. Poor start from Murtagh.
Outside off, Noor Ali taps it towards cover, sets off for a single but is sent back.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On middle and leg, helped through the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Wrong line, strays on the pads, Shahzad tickles it past short fine leg and gets another boundary.
FOUR! What a welcome. Full and wide outside off, Shahzad reaches out and slaps it over extra cover for a boundary!
TIM MURTAGH to bowl with the second new ball.
Another quick single. MS taps this to the right of short mid-wicket and sets off for a quick run. The fielder comes in from mid on and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
Nicely done. Pushes this with soft hands towards mid on and takes a quick run. Both openers are off the mark then.
Full and on middle, Mohammad flicks it behind square leg for a single to set things underway.
Fuller and wider outside off, slashed from the crease to cover.
Full and just outside off, Shahzad slightly opens the face of the bat and pushes the ball to point.
The players are out in the middle. Mohammad Shahzad and Noor Ali Zadran are the openers for Afghanistan. Peter Chase will start off proceedings to Shahzad. Here we go...

Ireland captain, WILLIAM PORTERFIELD says that he would looked to bat first as well. On the previous game, he admits that his team lost its way after a very good start. Hopes to get good partnerships today. On being asked as to what is that Ireland need to do to start winning, Porterfield says that his team has played good cricket in this tour and is not far from getting back to winnings ways. Informs that Ireland have been forced to make two changes in this game. Kevin O' Brien and Jacob Mulder are ruled out due to a niggle and have been replaced by Andy Balbirnie and Andy McBrine.

Afghanistan skipper, ASGHAR STANIZKAI says that the wicket looks good enough but later it becomes good for spin, Feels that 250 would be a good score. Informs that today, SHAFIQULLAH SHAFAQ is playing in place of Hashmatullah Shahidi.

TOSS - Porterfield calls it wrong again. AFGHANISTAN CHOOSE TO BAT ONCE MORE. Pretty surprising, considering that many teams would prefer bowling first in day games, to utilize the moisture early in the morning, but then the Afghans are confident in whatever they do. Ireland need to put up a team effort today.

PITCH REPORT - Chetan Sharma doing the pitch report feels that it is similar to the one which featured in the first ODI. Looks like a pretty good batting wicket, with a bit of grass to hold the surface. Might offer a bit of help for the fast bowlers in the first half an hour but then after that, the batters should have a say.
WEATHER - Another pleasant day in the offing. Summer has just set in but a cool breeze will help the players.

Hello and a warm welcome to the second of the 5-match ODI series between Afghanistan and Ireland in Noida. It has been one-way traffic this entire tour so far and after a terrific escape in the previous game, the Afghans must be sky-high on confidence. The Irish can still make a comeback, no doubt but are they mentally tough? They need that to regain some composure and draw level in this series. A loss today and even this series might go out of their hands.
